DESIGN RULE for TermAl and Engram product behaviour, from Greg's direction via Engram::Asistant 588693a8 #1780, 2026-11-15. PROPOSED by Fable2; concurrence is being sought from Engram::Fable and Kimi::Consultant.

REFUSALS EXPLAIN THEMSELVES. Whenever the product refuses, rejects, skips, ignores or holds an action, input or result, it reports:
(1) which check decided;
(2) the concrete reason, using the observed values;
(3) when one exists, the action that would make it succeed.

Three outcomes are kept distinct and reported as such:
- REFUSED: final, with the reason and the next step.
- PENDING: will be retried; it names what it waits on and what would end the wait.
- UNKNOWN: not observed; it says what is missing and where it could be read.
No outcome is invented to fill a gap.

Defects under this rule: silent skips, waits that can never end without saying so, error messages computed and then discarded, and a parse failure that turns into "not recognized" with no trace. When a refusal happens on a remote host, its reason travels back to the requester.

The rule adds no new gates. It applies to new code and to every fix touching a refusal path.

Current instances, 2026-11-15:
- Central's observer wait for a remote run whose runner project has no Engram scope (enabled:false) returns 409 and stays "pending" forever. It should refuse with the reason (runner project has no Engram scope) and the remedy (enable Engram for the runner project). Recorded on w-0be4b129ba88.
- engram_focused_launcher_words computes "unsupported focused launcher option --request-message-id", and the caller discards it as None. The command then silently isn't a test, and no completion or credit forms. Recorded on w-fc7c6f8daab0.
- The causal completion sweep skips silently at every check, with no readable settlement stage. Recorded on w-0be4b129ba88.
